title: What I learned driving the Slate electric truck prototype
gist: A first drive of Slate Auto's prototype electric truck finds it deliberately simple and utilitarian: manual windows and seats, a minimalist display, 8 s to 60 mph. The author expects American buyers to like it if Slate can reach mass production.

insights.claim: The Slate prototype has a minimalist digital display, manual seat and steering column adjustment, hand-set mirrors, a dash-slotted key fob, manual window winders and three climate dials, a deliberate contrast with feature-heavy modern vehicles.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: A de-contented, low-cost EV targets buyers fatigued by screen-heavy vehicles.

insights.claim: The Slate is a two-seat truck at 68 inches tall, with a 4,048 lb curb weight, 181 hp and 195 lb-ft motor, 0-60 mph in 8 seconds, and up to 1,500 lbs of bed payload using a De Dion rear axle and coil springs.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Performance is modest, slower than a Chevrolet Bolt, so the pitch rests on price and simplicity rather than speed.

insights.claim: The prototype had almost 6,000 miles and used hard shiny black plastic and Velcro from camouflage, so interior surfaces are not representative of production even though the layout is.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Material quality of the production version is unproven.

insights.claim: Default one-pedal driving with fixed lift-off regen was more aggressive at low speeds than any other recent EV the author drove, though easy to adapt to.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Minor tuning item that could be revised before production.

insights.claim: The author argues the Slate is the antithesis of what the auto industry, especially in North America, is currently offering and compares its simple honesty to a Fiat Panda.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Supports a demand thesis for cheap, utilitarian EVs against the trend of premium, tech-laden models.
insights.quote: “the Slate really is the antithesis (in a good way) of so much of what we are being offered by the automotive industry right now”

insights.claim: The author predicts Slate Auto will have a hit on its hands and that American drivers will like it, conditional on the company achieving mass production.
insights.speaker: Jonathan M. Gitlin
insights.so_what: Manufacturing scale-up, not product appeal, is identified as the main risk.
insights.quote: “Of course, having a compelling product is only part of the challenge for Slate; mass production still needs to happen.”
